manager.menuHint: Open the House Rules Manager to enable or disable individual house rules for this world.
manager.reloadNotice: House rules updated. Reload Foundry so every connected client applies the change.

example.title: Example House Rule (template)
example.hint: Disabled by default. Copy the houserules/_example folder to create a new house rule; this one only logs a message to the console when enabled, as a working template.

exhaustionOnDrop.title: Exhaustion after a Knockout
exhaustionOnDrop.hint: A player character who ends up at 0 HP gains one level of exhaustion the moment they are healed back above 0 HP - not the instant they drop. No cap per rest: every time they are brought back up is another level, and a character who is never healed above 0 HP gains nothing. Only affects player characters, not NPCs/allies.

moraleCheck.title: Morale Checks
moraleCheck.hint: Adds a leader token status and a half-HP/leader-down GM reminder for morale checks, plus a rollMoraleCheck() macro API (DC 10 Wisdom save) for targeted NPCs. Fleeing/surrendering stays your call.
moraleCheck.reminderHalfHp: Morale check reminder: {name} just dropped to half HP or less.
moraleCheck.reminderLeaderDown: Morale check reminder: {name} (marked as leader) was just dropped.
moraleCheck.noTargets: No targeted or selected NPC tokens to roll a morale check for.
moraleCheck.autoFail: {name} automatically fails its morale check (overwhelming odds).

lingeringInjury.title: Lingering Injury instead of Massive Damage death
lingeringInjury.hint: When a hit's leftover damage after dropping a PC to 0 HP would equal/exceed their HP max (the DMG's Massive Damage instant-death rule, which dnd5e does not automate), this rolls on the DMG's own Lingering Injuries table instead and applies it as an Active Effect - the part dnd5e can enforce (disadvantage, advantage, speed) is automated, the rest (repeated saving throws, decay over time) stays described for the table to apply. Player characters only. Remove the effect manually once resolved.
lingeringInjury.announcement: {name} takes a blow that should have been fatal - instead they're left with: {injury}.

eye.name: Lost Eye
eye.description: The blow destroys an eye, or leaves it useless.
eye.mechanic: Disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight and on ranged attack rolls. If no eyes remain after this injury, the character is blinded. Regenerate or equivalent magic restores the lost eye. (The ranged attack disadvantage is not automated: dnd5e keeps no such data on the actor, apply it by hand on ranged attacks.)

limb.name: Lost Arm or Hand
limb.description: The limb no longer answers, or is simply gone.
limb.mechanic: The character can no longer hold anything with two hands, and can hold only one object at a time. Regenerate or equivalent magic restores the lost limb. (Not automated: no Active Effect can restrict what a player holds, enforce it at the table.)

leg.name: Lost Foot or Leg
leg.description: The leg no longer carries the character's weight, or is gone.
leg.mechanic: Walking speed is halved. The character needs a cane, crutch, or prosthesis to move unless they already have a peg leg or similar. They fall prone after taking the Dash action, and have disadvantage on all Dexterity checks made to remain balanced. Regenerate or equivalent magic restores the lost limb. (The halved speed is automated; the cane/prosthesis, the fall after Dash, and the balance disadvantage are not.)

hobbled.name: Hobbled
hobbled.description: A limp that never quite goes away.
hobbled.mechanic: Walking speed reduced by 5 feet (1.5 m). After taking the Dash action, a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw: on a failure, the character falls prone. Magical healing removes the hobble. (The speed reduction is automated; the saving throw after Dash is not.)

internalInjury.name: Internal Injury
internalInjury.description: Something inside is no longer working right.
internalInjury.mechanic: Whenever the character attempts an action in combat, a DC 15 Constitution saving throw: on a failure, they lose that action and can't take reactions until the start of their next turn. Heals with magical healing, or after ten days of complete rest. (Not automated: it's a saving throw repeated on every action, keep track of it at the table.)

brokenRibs.name: Broken Ribs
brokenRibs.description: Every deep breath is a stab of pain.
brokenRibs.mechanic: Same effect as Internal Injury, but the Constitution saving throw is DC 10. (Not automated, for the same reason.)

horribleScar.name: Horrible Scar
horribleScar.description: A mark that draws every eye.
horribleScar.mechanic: Disadvantage on Charisma (Persuasion) checks, advantage on Charisma (Intimidation) checks. Only 6th-level or higher magic (such as heal or regenerate) removes the scar.

festeringWound.name: Festering Wound
festeringWound.description: The wound will not close, and it is getting worse.
festeringWound.mechanic: The character's hit point maximum decreases by 1 for every 24 hours the wound persists. If it drops to 0, the character dies. Heals with magical healing, or if someone tends the wound with a DC 15 Wisdom (Medicine) check once every 24 hours: after ten successes, it heals. (Not automated: it's a decay over time, track it at the table - nothing here counts the days passing.)

minorScar.name: Minor Scar
minorScar.mechanic: No mechanical effect. Only 6th-level or higher magic (such as heal or regenerate) removes the scar.

slowNaturalHealing.title: Slow Natural Healing
slowNaturalHealing.hint: A long rest no longer restores hit points on its own: the only way back up is spending Hit Dice (the DMG's Slow Natural Healing variant). Everything else about the rest is unchanged - Hit Dice, spell slots, item uses and the level of exhaustion it removes. Applies to every actor, NPCs included.
slowNaturalHealing.spendLabel: Spend available Hit Dice before the rest
slowNaturalHealing.spendHint: Rolls Hit Dice until you are nearly at full HP or you run out, before the rest hands any of them back. Under the 2024 rules a long rest returns every spent die, so healing this way usually costs nothing - still better than leaving dice unused overnight.
